title: A coordinate lowers fibre dimension over a dense principal open
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, with both $R$ and $S$ of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Fix an integer $d\ge1$. Suppose every scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] of $\operatorname{Spec}(S)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ [def-pc-scheme] has topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] at most $d$. Then there exist $a\in S$ and $f\in R$ such that $f$ belongs to no minimal prime ideal of $R$ (a minimal prime is a prime ideal containing no strictly smaller prime ideal), and every fibre of the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(S_f)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R_f[t])$ induced by $t\mapsto a/1$ has dimension at most $d-1$. Here $R_f=R[1/f]$ and $S_f=S[1/\varphi(f)]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], and $R_f[t]$ is the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Empty spectra have dimension $-\infty$ and are allowed.

source.place: Tag 0GTG, label lemma-weak-relative-noether-normalization, proof lines 8832–8871 (the generic-point argument, shrinking the base, and prime avoidance); this is the intermediate dense-principal-open assertion, before the induction and power perturbation.

proof.text: Because $R$ and $S$ are finite type over $\mathbf Z$, they are Noetherian (the integers are Noetherian and finite type algebras preserve Noetherianity), so $S$ has finitely many minimal primes by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes]. For each minimal prime $\mathfrak q$ of $S$, put $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$; $\mathfrak q$ is a generic point of the corresponding finite-type fibre over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Applying the dimension-at-a-point formula [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-local-ring-trdeg] to that fibre, whose local ring at this generic point has dimension zero, gives the fibre-component dimension $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. Let $\mathfrak q_1,\ldots,\mathfrak q_r$ be the minimal primes for which this value is the maximal value $d$, and put $\mathfrak p_i=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q_i)$. The remaining minimal primes have $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(\mathfrak q)<d$. The $\mathfrak q_i$ are pairwise incomparable. Apply [lem-trf-finite-prime-transcendental-coordinate] with $B=S$, $J=S$, and $k_i=\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)$ (embedded in $\kappa(\mathfrak q_i)$) to obtain $a\in S$ whose image is transcendental over $\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)$ for every $i$. If the list is empty, take $a=0$; then every generic fibre component already has dimension at most $d-1.

source.place: Tag 0GTG, proof lines 8832–8843 (minimal maximal-dimensional fibre components and the transcendental coordinate; Tag 00P1 for the dimension calculation)

proof.text:
Let $f_a:\operatorname{Spec}(S)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R[t])$ be induced by $t\mapsto a$. The locus where the local dimension of an $f_a$-fibre is at most $d-1$ is open by [lem-weil-pbc-local-fibre-dimension-open]. We verify that it contains every generic point $\mathfrak q$ of $\operatorname{Spec}(S)$. Put $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ and let $\xi=f_a(\mathfrak q)$, so $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\subseteq\kappa(\xi)\subseteq\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-local-ring-trdeg] to the finite-type fibre over $\kappa(\xi)$ at its generic point $\mathfrak q$ gives $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(f_a^{-1}(\xi))=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(\xi)}\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. The tower formula [lem-sbc-transcendence-degree-tower] gives
$$\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(\mathfrak q)=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(\xi)}\kappa(\mathfrak q)+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(\xi).$$
For a selected $\mathfrak q_i$, transcendence of $a$ makes $\kappa(\xi)=\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)(a)$ and the last degree equal to $1$, while the first step gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)}\kappa(\mathfrak q_i)=d$, so the new fibre dimension at $\mathfrak q_i$ is $d-1$. For every unselected minimal prime, the first step gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(\mathfrak q)<d$, and the displayed equality makes $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(\xi)}\kappa(\mathfrak q)\leq\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(\mathfrak q)<d$. Thus all generic points lie in the open locus; call it $U$.

source.place: Tag 0GTG, proof lines 8844–8855, using Morphisms Tag 02FZ (openness of bounded fibre dimension)

proof.text: Set $T=\operatorname{Spec}(S)\setminus U$ with its reduced closed subscheme structure. The generic points of every generic fibre of $\operatorname{Spec}(S)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ lie in $U$: if $x$ is a generic point of the fibre over a minimal prime $\eta$ of $R$, every generization $x'$ of $x$ maps to a generization of $\eta$, hence to $\eta$, so $x'$ lies in the same fibre and $x'=x$; thus $x$ is a generic point of $\operatorname{Spec}(S)$ and lies in $U$ by Step 2, so every irreducible component of a generic fibre of $T\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ is a proper closed subspace of a component of the original fibre. Any strict chain of irreducible closed subsets in such a proper component extends by its ambient generic point, hence has length at most $d-1$. Thus each generic fibre of $T$ has dimension at most $d-1$.

source.place: Tag 0GTG, proof lines 8852–8859 (removing the generic points lowers the generic-fibre dimension)

proof.text:
The morphism $T\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ is of finite type because $T$ is defined by a quotient of the finite-type $R$-algebra $S$. Let $C_1,\ldots,C_m$ be the finitely many irreducible components of $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$, and for each $i$ let
$$W_i=\operatorname{Spec}(R)\setminus\bigcup_{j\ne i}C_j.$$
Each $W_i$ is a nonempty irreducible open with generic point $\eta_i$, and the union of the $W_i$ is dense. Restrict $T$ to $T_i=T\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(R)}W_i$. If the generic fibre of $T_i\to W_i$ is nonempty of dimension $n_i\le d-1$, apply [lem-trf-generic-fibre-dimension-neighborhood] to obtain a nonempty open $V_i\subseteq W_i$ on which all fibres have dimension $n_i$. If the generic fibre is empty, apply [lem-sbc-generic-fibre-closed-avoidance] to the restricted morphism at $\eta_i$ with the closed subset $T_i$ itself; since $\overline{\{\eta_i\}}=W_i$, this gives a nonempty open $V_i\subseteq W_i$ on which all fibres are empty. The union $V=\bigcup_i V_i$ is an open dense subset of $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$, and every fibre of $T$ over $V$ has dimension at most $d-1.

source.place: Tag 0GTG, proof lines 8857–8863, using Tags 05F7 and 054W

proof.text:
For $q$ in the affine line over $V$, write $F=f_a^{-1}(q)$. Consider any strict chain of irreducible closed subsets
$$C_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq C_m\subseteq F$$
and let $\xi$ be the generic point of its top member $C_m$. If $\xi\in T$, then $C_m\subseteq T_q$ because $T$ is closed, so $m\le\dim T_q$. Let $\mathfrak p\in V$ be the image of $q$ in $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$; the fibre $T_q$ is, as a topological space, a subspace of the fibre $T_{\mathfrak p}$. A subspace has Krull dimension at most that of the ambient space (elementary: if $Z_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq Z_m$ are irreducible closed in the subspace, their closures in $T_{\mathfrak p}$ are irreducible and closed, and they remain distinct because each $Z_i$ is the trace on the subspace of its closure). Hence $m\le\dim T_q\le\dim T_{\mathfrak p}\le d-1$ by Step 4. If $\xi\in U$, apply [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] to the finite-type $\kappa(q)$-scheme $F$ and $C_m$ to get $\dim C_m=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(q)}\kappa_F(\xi)$. The 00P1 formula [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-local-ring-trdeg] gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(q)}\kappa_F(\xi)\le\dim_\xi F$, and the definition of $U$ gives $\dim_\xi F\le d-1$. Hence $m\le\dim C_m\le d-1$ in either case, so every such fibre has dimension at most $d-1$. Since $V$ is dense, its closed complement $V(I)$ contains no generic point of $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$, so $I$ lies in no minimal prime; $R$ is Noetherian and has finitely many minimal primes [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes], so prime avoidance [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance] applied to the ideal defining the closed complement of $V$ gives an element $f\in R$ outside every minimal prime with $D(f)\subseteq V$. Localizing the base and source at $f$ identifies the fibres over $\operatorname{Spec}(R_f[t])$ with the fibres over $D(f)$, using the localization convention [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Therefore $a$ and $f$ satisfy the required conclusion.

split_report.summary: Split the intermediate generic-principal-open assertion in Stacks Tag 0GTG into the finite-prime simultaneous-transcendence input, the generic-fibre dimension-neighborhood input, and the existing empty-generic-fibre shrinking input. The five proof steps then follow the source: choose a transcendental coordinate on maximal-dimensional minimal fibre components, use openness of local fibre dimension, remove the generic points to lower the complement dimension, shrink over each irreducible base component, and choose a principal open avoiding all minimal primes. The target statement and hypotheses are unchanged.
